chunks: ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man whom al-qiṣāṣ killed: is there diyah for him?
So he said: “If that were so, al-qiṣāṣ would not be carried out against anyone. And whoever is killed by the hadd, there is no diyah for him.”

key_terms.الْحَدُّ: a prescribed legal punishment set by the Sacred Law
key_terms.الْقِصَاصُ: lawful retaliation in kind for homicide or bodily injury
key_terms.دِيَةٌ: financial blood-compensation paid in cases of wrongful killing or injury
key_terms.رَجُلٍ: a man, the subject of the legal question
key_terms.لَا دِيَةَ لَهُ: no blood-money is due for him in this legal circumstance

ai.seo_question: Is there diyah for someone who is killed through qiṣāṣ or hadd punishment in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling from Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that a person executed through lawful retaliation or through a prescribed hadd punishment is not entitled to diyah. The report emphasizes the functioning of the justice system, indicating that financial compensation does not apply where death occurs through a divinely sanctioned legal penalty.
